guidance: Central Texas has two growing seasons, spring and fall, separated by a summer heat gap in July-August when most fruiting crops stall. If spring goes wrong, try again in the fall.
Hill County soils are heavy Blackland/Grand Prairie clay, alkaline, with caliche in places. Drainage is slow: raise or amend beds and water deeply but infrequently.
Water deeply so moisture reaches 3 inches or more. A brief shower rarely reaches the roots. Above 95F expect blossom drop on tomatoes, peppers and beans regardless of watering.
Use 30-50% shade cloth, or afternoon shade after 3 pm, through July and August.
Mulch 2-3 inches to hold moisture and moderate soil temperature; keep it off stems.
Start warm-season transplants indoors 6-8 weeks before the mid-March transplant window, i.e. late January.
Seed cole crops indoors Aug 1-15 for transplanting Aug 20 - Sep 15.
source: AgriLife Fall Vegetable Gardening Guide (Region III / Zone 8)

guidance: Harden off transplants over 7-14 days, increasing outdoor hours each day and starting in shade.
Average first fall frost is around Nov 15-25. Cover or harvest tender crops when a freeze warning is issued.
Average last spring frost is around Mar 9-31. Hold warm-season transplants until the risk passes.
